To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Finnish Paper Workers’ Union (Paperiliitto, PL) has defended acquired rights in its representation of its constituency.
the Finnish Paper Workers Union (FPWU) has defended the acquired rights of its members and perhaps has narrowed its representation of the diverse constituencies in the Finnish paper sector.
the Finnish paper industry has undergone a process of restructuring and that this restructuring has been reflected in the Finnish Paper Workers’ Union.

the following question: How did the Finnish Paper Workers Union (Paperiliit) represent its constituency during a period of change in its industrial relations?
the question of whose constituency the union has represented in the outsourcing conflict.
the representativeness of the Paper Workers' union in relation to its members, the paper industry, and the Finnish labour market.

outsourcing has been a complex issue in the paper industry, and the Paper Workers' Unions' stance has been ambivalent.
the Paper Workers' union has been a representative actor, although it has not always been the most representative one.
outsourcing has not been an issue of the union, but of its members.

the union is not only a representative organization, but also a political organization.
